summary: This version of the temperature converter adds a finally block, so a farewell message always prints when the program finishes — whether the conversion succeeded or an exception was caught. The rest of the program still loops until the user types a numeric Celsius value inside the allowed range.

lines.text: Declaring the Scanner inside the parentheses of the try makes it a try-with-resources, so Java closes the scanner for you when the block ends. This is the same "clean up after the meal" idea the finally block handles for anything Java cannot close automatically.

lines.code: System.out.print("Out of range. Enter a value between -273.15 and 100: ");
lines.text: An out-of-range temperature is not treated as a crash-worthy error; the user is simply asked again, which is the friendlier choice for input typed by a person.
This inner catch handles only the specific failure of Double.parseDouble on text that is not a number, leaving the outer catch free to deal with anything else that might go wrong.
The outer catch is the safety net for unexpected problems, and catching the general Exception type means nothing escapes without a readable message.
The finally block is the only change from the previous version, and it runs no matter what happens above it — successful conversion, caught exception, or otherwise.
Because it lives in finally, this closing message is guaranteed, which is exactly where you would put code that releases files, database connections, or other resources.
